line: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Bg7 Bf4 Nxd5 Nxd5 Qxd5 Bg3 c5 dxc5
teaches: When the centre pawn finally captures, look down the file it just left — the capture that wins a pawn can open the line your queen was already standing on, and a file opened onto their back rank matters more than the pawn that opened it.
explains: The pawn's capture on c5 has cleared the d-file from top to bottom: the queen on d5 now looks straight down at the queen on d1 with nothing between them. The pawn can be regained at leisure — the open file and the exposed first rank are the real change on the board.

line: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Bg7 Bf4 Nxd5 Nxd5 Qxd5 Bg3 c5 dxc5 Qxc5 Rc1 Qa5+
teaches: When the enemy king is still in the centre, a queen check that can only be answered by a block is a lever — the block invites the trade, and the recapture drags the king to a working square of your choosing, so the endgame starts with their king already misplaced.
explains: The queen checks from a5 down the open diagonal to the king on e1. There is no comfortable answer: blocking invites the queen trade, and the recapture pulls the king into the middle of the board with pieces still on. Every later idea gains a move against a king that has to watch its step.
